questions.prompt: What must exist before any penetration testing begins?

options.text: Explicit written authorization from the system owner, with defined scope
A public disclosure of the findings

questions.explanation: Authorization and scope are what separate ethical hacking from a crime; the same actions without permission are illegal.

questions.prompt: Order the phases of a penetration test.
questions.explanation: A test moves from reconnaissance and enumeration to careful exploitation and post-exploitation, ending in the report and confirmation retest.

questions.prompt: Match each engagement type to its description.

pairs.right: Tester has partial knowledge (e.g. a user account)
Stealthy adversary simulation testing detection & response

questions.explanation: Black/grey/white box vary the tester's prior knowledge; a red team runs a goal-oriented, stealthy simulation.

questions.prompt: The real deliverable of a penetration test is not the exploit but the ____.
questions.explanation: Value comes from fixing what's found; the prioritized report with remediation guidance is the product.

questions.prompt: Which must a professional engagement define up front? Select all that apply.

options.text: Scope (what is in and out of bounds)
Rules of Engagement (allowed techniques, timing, stop conditions)

questions.explanation: Scope, Rules of Engagement, and signed authorization bound the test legally and safely.

questions.prompt: How does a penetration test complement a vulnerability scan?

options.text: The scan gives automated breadth; the pen test adds manual depth, chaining flaws to prove impact
They are the same and either alone is complete
A pen test replaces the need to ever scan
Scanning proves exploitability better than a pen test

questions.explanation: Scanning covers many known issues automatically; a pen test manually chains weaknesses to demonstrate real, exploitable impact.
